idiom_name: duck-typed nodes: shared method names, containers hold a list
implementation_notes: Python does not need the shared base class: as python-patterns.guide puts it, container and content can share only an interface - or nothing but a matching method name - so the pattern reduces to objects answering the operation plus a children list on containers. Introduce a common ABC or a typing.Protocol only when the protocol must be enforced or dispatched on; the standard library already ships ready-made composites in xml.etree.ElementTree (Element.append/iter over a child tree) and the ast module, which is usually the better answer than writing another tree. Use the dataclass-union variant instead when the node set is closed and exhaustiveness is wanted.
pitfalls: A typo'd method name fails only at call time deep inside the recursion; name the protocol in a typing.Protocol and check it with a type checker when other teams build the tree.
A mutable default argument (children=[]) is shared by every node - the classic Python aliasing bug.
Recursive walks hit the interpreter recursion limit (about 1000 frames); deep or untrusted trees need an explicit stack or an iterator.

variants.name: Frozen dataclass union with exhaustive match (closed node set)
variants.idiom_name: frozen dataclasses in a union + match with assert_never
variants.implementation_notes: A closed node set can be modelled as frozen dataclasses in a union type, with each operation a recursive function that match-es on the variants and ends with case _: assert_never(node) so a type checker reports any unhandled variant. Nodes become immutable values, so an edit rebuilds the path instead of mutating a child list, and no base class is involved at all. Prefer this when the node set is closed and traversal is written as a library of functions; use the duck-typed variant when node types must be extended from outside.
variants.code_sketch:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import assert_never

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class File: name: str; bytes: int

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Dir: name: str; children: tuple["Node", ...]

Node = File | Dir

def size(node: Node) -> int:
    match node:
        case File(_, b): return b
        case Dir(_, children): return sum(size(c) for c in children)
        case _: assert_never(node)
pitfalls: frozen=True is shallow: a list field is still mutable, so children must be tuples for real immutability.
assert_never only fires when a type checker runs; without mypy/pyright the exhaustiveness claim is decorative.
Positional patterns bind by field order, so reordering dataclass fields silently changes the meaning of every match.
